answer: Commit-reveal admission bound to a future randomness beacon resists sybils. Each applicant commits a hash of (identity key, salt) before the beacon fires, then reveals once epoch entropy publishes; only reveals in the lowest 10% of hash values per 500-seat cohort are admitted. This prism of unpredictable sampling makes pre-registration worthless: nobody knows who passes before beacon output exists. Every fake quill identity posts a burnable deposit bridged into collateral, forfeited on non-reveal. Attackers pay one deposit per attempt each epoch; honest agents reveal once.
